findings.condition: Operating the internal wideband CAN bus (ECU brain CAN2 transceiver U21 plus wideband module transceivers) without user-added external termination.

evidence.locator: symbol uuid d69380f9-5487-4782-9ce9-0690df62e543: R36 value 120, (dnp yes), (in_bom no); text 'n.p.' uuid 98ed307b at (113.03 76.2); wiring ties R36 pins to CAN2+ (y=83.82) and CAN2- (y=88.9)
dnp_refs includes R36 and R37; footprint R36 (uuid starting ed50429c pad entries) dnp=true with pad1 net /CAN2+ and pad2 net /CAN2- at ~(175.0, 142.1)
'Dual wideband O2 sensor controllers ... (connected internally to CAN bus #2)'

findings.mechanism: With both 120R resistors unpopulated, differential termination is only the transceivers' internal bias (tens of kilohms). Recessive-state transitions must discharge the bus capacitance (including the four populated 47p filter caps C29/C30/C33/C34 plus trace and transceiver capacitance) through that high impedance, giving microsecond-scale edges that corrupt bits at typical CAN rates; reflections are also undamped. Internal wideband communication would be unreliable or nonfunctional unless termination exists elsewhere.
findings.reasoning: The DNP is clearly intentional (schematic 'n.p.' note), which suggests the designers expect termination elsewhere, possibly external on the harness since /CAN2+ also appears on module-connector pads (J2 pad 73 per DRC items). But the packet contains no evidence of any populated termination anywhere on CAN2, and the README presents the wideband link as internal. If the bus is used as documented with no external nodes, it is unterminated and likely nonfunctional. Because the intended system-level termination strategy is unstated and the root schematic is unavailable, this is reported as a concern rather than a defect, but it directly challenges the packet's stated scope of internal dual-wideband CAN termination.
findings.title: Both internal CAN2 (wideband bus) 120R terminations are DNP; bus has no populated termination
